guarantees.promise: No payout is ever larger than the contractor's share of the client payment it cites.
Nobody is paid with money that has not arrived: every payout points at a client payment PayPal confirmed.
In a month, contractors are paid no more than the monthly cap that was in force.
Someone who is not on the rules is never paid, and neither is work that is not on the rules, whatever the story.
A request the rules refused never reaches PayPal: it has no order, no payout and no capture.
A request is never paid twice, however often it is repeated, retried or replayed.
Once approved, a request cannot be changed: the payee, amount, proof, job and funding are locked and signed.
Every payment that moved had the owner's tap or a standing rule the owner signed.
A passkey tap with no stored signature is red. An owner key and a demo tap are amber. An older row is grey and marked legacy.
Every member has a valid role, at least one active owner exists, and expired or revoked members cannot act.
Passkey approvals and step-up grants require authentic cryptographic signatures with user verification.
Published rules match the warrant schema and passkey-published rules keep their cryptographic binding.
Every pause, resume, and safety breaker event on the ledger is signed by the server key.
Server signing keys have valid PEM structure and SHA-256 fingerprints matching /.well-known/mandate-keys.json.
No AI can approve, pay, change the rules, or call a PayPal tool that moves money.
A model's sentence never claims that money moved, or states a figure nobody supplied: it is taken back.
While Mandate is paused nothing runs on its own, and the history of pauses is signed.
A receipt can be checked in a browser without asking this server.
The dashboard has no path to PayPal: it is handed rows, and its agent module imports nothing of Mandate's.
When PayPal is slow or down, a repeatable call is retried, an unrepeatable one is not, and a person is told which.
